discovery: High-resolution resonant inelastic X-ray scattering (RIXS) as a momentum-resolved probe of collective spin and charge excitations, revealing paramagnons and incipient charge order in cuprate superconductors

nominees.name: Bernhard Keimer
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute for Solid State Research, Stuttgart, Germany

subfield: Experimental condensed matter physics / X-ray spectroscopy of quantum materials
motivation: Braicovich and Ghiringhelli conceived and built soft-X-ray RIXS spectrometers (AXES, SAXES, ERIXS) with resolving power improved by orders of magnitude, turning RIXS into a quantitative, momentum-resolved probe of magnetic and charge excitations. With Keimer they used it to settle long-standing questions in high-temperature superconductivity. They showed that damped spin excitations (paramagnons) persist with substantial spectral weight across the entire doping range of cuprates (Le Tacon et al., Nature Physics 2011). They also discovered that incommensurate charge-density-wave order competes with superconductivity in YBa2Cu3O6+x (Ghiringhelli et al., Science 2012), which established charge order as a universal feature of the cuprates. The technique is now central to every major synchrotron and XFEL program and has transformed the study of iridates, nickelates and other correlated materials. This work shows how a new instrument, built to see collective electron behaviour directly, can reshape a field.
